cohort: 153 pregnant women aged 18-40 years with term pregnancies (37-42 weeks gestation) and spontaneous labor.
finding: Abnormal umbilical cord length (both short and long) is associated with an increased possibility of fetal asphyxia (decreased APGAR score) and fetal mortality (stillbirths).
mod_finding: The study concluded that umbilical cord length was not significantly associated with maternal outcomes, including mode of birth.
